cases.name: Duel Anchors
cases.challenge: Keep first-person Digital Duels readable in crowded, handcrafted levels.
cases.decision: Use tested Player/Guard anchor pairs and brief glitch transitions instead of dynamically finding combat space. Restore positions and security states afterward.

cases.name: Manual Backdoor
cases.challenge: Let players resume unfinished infiltrations without making failed operations reversible or saving the entire dynamic world.
cases.decision: Players physically reach safe terminals to install or update one Backdoor. Recovery restores persistent progress, not temporary guard positions or camera spoofing.

cases.name: Guard Hearing
cases.challenge: Make noisy movement matter without turning every sound into an unfair instant alarm.
cases.decision: Movement generates simple distance-based noise events. Guards investigate the last-heard position; only visual confirmation triggers an intrusion alarm.

cases.name: Security Subsystems
cases.challenge: Make hacking change infiltration choices rather than automatically disable every security measure.
cases.decision: Exploit a nearby vulnerable device to access its connected subsystem. Camera access reveals detection zones and enables individual feed spoofing on Normal/Hard; access-control systems can unlock restricted doors and windows.

logs.title: Game Design Document Completed
logs.summary: The foundation of Stole This Game is now documented. Core mechanics, mission structure, progression, and development milestones have been defined.
logs.body: The GDD establishes the scope of the project: three handcrafted locations, stealth-hacking gameplay, security subsystems, Duel Anchors, Manual Backdoor, and a campaign followed by additional contracts. The next challenge is turning these designs into a playable experience.
